hook: You get a notification. You check it. There is nothing important. You scroll anyway.
topic: How notifications trigger the full scroll loop
body:
**You get a notification. You check it. There is nothing important. You scroll anyway.**

That sequence is not random. It was designed. The notification is not there to deliver information — it is there to generate a pickup. Once you are in the app, the content environment takes over. Infinite scroll removes the stopping point. You scroll because the architecture of the platform gives you no natural place to stop.

Books have endings. TV episodes have credits. Conversations have pauses. Infinite scroll was specifically engineered to eliminate the equivalent moment. The designer who built pull-to-refresh — the gesture that mimics a slot machine lever — later said publicly that he no longer uses it himself.

You were not going to stop on your own. The system was not built for that.

The intervention starts with a notification audit. Ninety percent of your notifications carry zero useful information and every one of them is a trained entry point into the loop.

Go to settings tonight. Turn off every notification that is not a direct message from a real person. That is the first structural move.

Full audit framework is in the link in bio.
